record.context_brief: Systematic study of non-convex expectation-parameter spaces
record.original_question: For exponential families, are there systematic studies of cases where the space of expectation parameters is non-convex, and if not, can such a theory be developed?

evidence.quote: Efron [32] found an example of an exponential family in which the space of expectation parameters is not convex. Are there systematic studies on this phenomenon? If not, can we develop?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a measurable space with a $\sigma$-finite reference measure $\nu$, and let $T:\mathcal{X}\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be a measurable statistic. The associated exponential family is the set of probability densities
$$p_\theta(x)=\exp\bigl(\langle \theta, T(x)\rangle - \psi(\theta)\bigr),\qquad \theta\in\Theta,$$
where $\Theta=\{\theta\in\mathbb{R}^d : \psi(\theta):=\log\int_\mathcal{X}\exp\langle\theta,T(x)\rangle\,d\nu(x)<\infty\}$ is the natural parameter space (which is always convex), and the expectation parameter space is
$$M=\{\mathbb{E}_\theta[T(X)] : \theta\in\Theta\}\subset\mathbb{R}^d.$$
While in standard regular cases $M$ is open and convex, there exist exponential families for which $M$ fails to be convex.

Develop a systematic theory describing the class of exponential families whose expectation parameter space $M$ is non-convex. In particular: characterize, in terms of the sufficient statistic $T$, the dominating measure $\nu$, and the geometry of $\Theta$, necessary and sufficient conditions under which $M$ is non-convex; describe the possible topological and geometric shapes that $M$ can take in such cases; and analyze the consequences of non-convexity for maximum likelihood estimation, the existence and uniqueness of the MLE, and the information-geometric structure (dual flatness, Bregman divergence, Legendre transform $\theta\leftrightarrow\mu$) of the family.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located Efron's example and standard treatments (Efron 1978, Efron 2018/2022) which note that the natural parameter space is always convex, and that pathological exponential families with non-convex expectation parameter spaces exist, but no systematic theory of such non-convex mean-parameter spaces appears in the standard literature. The question of building a general framework therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Geometry of Exponential Families (Efron, 1978)
status_evidence.snippet: Efron's foundational geometric paper defining the natural and expectation parameter spaces for multivariate exponential families.
status_evidence.claim: Provides Efron's geometric treatment, where examples of non-convex expectation parameter spaces originate.

status_evidence.title: Exponential Families in Theory and Practice (Efron, 2018)
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatment of exponential families; discusses natural and mean parameter spaces but does not give a systematic theory of non-convex expectation parameter spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference treats convex regular cases; no systematic theory of non-convex M is developed.

status_evidence.title: Statistical exponential families: A digest with flash cards
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of exponential families covering natural parameter space convexity and basic mean parameter properties.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys standard properties; does not address non-convex mean parameter spaces systematically.
